note: Reviewed fixtures for the planner. Each case states what a correct plan must do, not which exact steps it must contain, so the set survives registry changes. `reviewed` records whether a domain reviewer has confirmed the expectation; unreviewed cases are the author's judgement and are scored but flagged.

fields.route: the protocol the composed plan must land on
fields.rerouted_from: the route it must have started from, when a constraint changes it
fields.extract: constraints the brief must capture from the question
fields.must_include: modules whose absence would make the plan wrong
fields.must_exclude: modules that would be wrong for this case
fields.must_exclude_families: method families no step may belong to
fields.order: pairs [a, b] where a must come before b for scientific reasons
fields.target: the protein the question is about, or null when there is none
fields.unsupported: true when no protocol should be offered
fields.viable: false when the plan must be conditional on something the user has not supplied
fields.metal: true when the question involves a metal centre
fields.must_cover: groups of alternatives; the plan must contain at least one from each, for expectations about the science rather than a particular module id

cases.question: Find inhibitors of EGFR in human; 500 measured compounds, no usable structure, CPU only, two days, no docking or MD
cases.why: The worked example from the planning review: every constraint must survive and change the route.

cases.question: Analyse my existing EGFR trajectory; do not run docking or virtual screening
cases.why: Work already done is an input, not something to repeat; the excluded family must not appear.

cases.question: Find selective EGFR inhibitors that spare ERBB2
cases.why: Both proteins must survive, in their distinct roles, and the panel work must appear.

cases.question: My fragment screen gave 40 hits, which should I grow?
cases.why: The screen is complete; the plan must start from the hits and verify them, not re-select a library.

cases.question: I do not want FEP. Improve potency of my EGFR analogues using measured SAR
cases.why: The excluded method must go and the target must stay EGFR, not be misread from the prose.

cases.question: Find inhibitors of Aurora B in human
cases.why: The specific alias must beat the broader one; AURKA is the wrong kinase.

cases.question: Find inhibitors of EGFR in guinea pig
cases.why: Longest organism phrase wins; 'pig' inside 'guinea pig' is the wrong species.

cases.question: What is the weather tomorrow?
cases.why: Out of scope must produce no recommended workflow at all.

cases.question: Improve the potency of my series
cases.why: 'Improve' contains 'mpro'; boundary-aware aliasing must not invent a coronavirus protease.

cases.question: Find inhibitors of EGFR in human
cases.why: The default structure-based campaign, with its two controls present.

cases.question: I have 500 measured compounds for CDK2; build an activity model
cases.why: A model is not a model without a deployment-matched split and an applicability domain.

cases.question: Rank these EGFR analogues with FEP
cases.why: Free energy predictions need a retrospective check and a convergence check before they are believed.

cases.question: Run MD on my EGFR complex and tell me if it is stable
cases.why: A stability claim requires replicates and a predefined observable, not one trajectory.

cases.question: Conformational sampling of CYP3A4 to find cryptic pockets
cases.why: The observable is named first and convergence is proved before an ensemble is used.

cases.question: Why is my series hitting the wrong kinase?
cases.why: Selectivity is decided by comparing pockets, not by the primary target alone.

cases.question: Design a PROTAC for BRD4 using VHL
cases.why: A degrader needs the ternary complex and a mechanism proof, not just two binders.

cases.question: I have missense variants and 39 mutations, what to do to analyse mutants vs WT
cases.why: The reported failure: WT must not be read as Wilms tumour protein.

cases.question: Network pharmacology study of Aloysia citrodora against Parkinson's disease
cases.why: A plant name is study context, never a protein target.

cases.question: Plan a synthesis route for this molecule
cases.why: Routes are only useful if the building blocks are real and a chemist has looked.

cases.question: ADMET and hERG risk for my compound set
cases.why: Predicted liabilities mean nothing outside the applicability domain.

cases.question: Design a nanobody against this epitope
cases.why: Developability is designed in early, not discovered after affinity maturation.

cases.question: Generate new scaffolds for KRAS G12C
cases.why: Generated molecules get the same validation as any other compound source.

cases.question: Which target should I pick for Alzheimer's disease?
cases.why: Tractability and safety are part of target choice, not later surprises.

cases.question: Which PDB entry should I use for EGFR?
cases.why: Structure choice is ranked on evidence, with a prediction fallback stated.

cases.question: Fragment based design against this pocket
cases.why: Fragment hits are confirmed orthogonally and ligand efficiency is held as a constraint.

cases.question: Improve potency in my EGFR lead series using measured SAR
cases.why: Optimisation watches properties and synthesisability alongside potency.

cases.question: i wanna optimize geometry of palladium bound ligand
cases.why: The reported failure: a geometry optimisation is quantum chemistry, not lead optimisation.

cases.question: i wanna parametrize a gold containing ligand it's Au 3+
cases.why: The reported failure: gold was absent from the metal list and no protocol covered parameterisation.

cases.question: Work out the mechanism of this palladium catalysed step and the barrier
cases.why: A barrier is meaningless without a confirmed transition state and the competing pathway.

cases.question: Predict the pKa of my compound
cases.why: Absolute computed pKa is unreliable; the plan must calibrate against measured values.

cases.question: Dock hydroxamates into HDAC6 and spare HDAC1
cases.why: A zinc metalloenzyme with an off-target: metal setup, panel work and the chelator liability.

cases.question: Simulate the stability of a zinc finger protein
cases.why: A metal site needs parameters before simulation, but a zinc finger has no chelating warhead to hold liable.

cases.question: What is the best structure for a copper-binding protein?
cases.why: Judging a structure includes validating the metal in it, but nothing here is being docked or simulated.

cases.question: Engineer this thermophilic esterase to survive 70C without losing turnover
cases.why: Stability is routinely bought with activity; the plan must test for that rather than assume it.

cases.question: Design a cyclic peptide binder for this protein surface
cases.why: Peptides fail on liabilities more often than on affinity, so those come before optimisation.

cases.question: Find me the competitive landscape for KRAS inhibitors
cases.why: The reported failure: screening vocabulary, and not a screening campaign.

cases.question: Build a focused screening library for this target
cases.why: Every count downstream is wrong until the structures are standardised and deduplicated.

cases.question: How do I benchmark my scoring function?
cases.why: A benchmark without a trivial baseline on the same split is not interpretable.

cases.question: Find hits for CDK2 without docking or MD
cases.why: Two excluded families, both absolute.

cases.question: Find inhibitors of EGFR without a structure
cases.why: The absence must be read whether or not an adjective sits in front of the noun.

cases.question: Simulate a zinc finger protein without force field parameterisation
cases.why: A negation must cover every method word it runs across, not stop at the first.

cases.question: Find inhibitors of EGFR without docking but use MD
cases.why: A negation must not swallow the positive clause that follows it.

cases.question: Screen for CDK2 inhibitors, CPU only, within two days
cases.why: Limits the planner cannot act on must be reported as not applied, not silently dropped.

cases.question: Who first discovered EGFR inhibitors?
cases.why: Vocabulary of a workflow without a request for one.

cases.question: How much do EGFR inhibitors cost per gram?
cases.why: Procurement, not a computational workflow.

cases.question: Which journal should I submit my docking paper to?
cases.why: Contains a method word and asks nothing the registry covers.

cases.question: Help me with EGFR drug discovery
cases.why: A target and a field, with no requested outcome, must not be filled in with hit discovery.

cases.question: Design a drug discovery workflow for Alzheimer's
cases.why: Neither generative design nor hit discovery; the goal is unspecified.

cases.question: What is the gold standard for docking validation?
cases.why: This field says 'gold standard' constantly and never means gold.

cases.question: Lead optimisation of my compound series
cases.why: Lead is an element name and a stage of a project; here it is the stage.

cases.question: Find calcium channel blockers for hypertension
cases.why: A calcium channel is a target, not a coordination chemistry problem.

cases.question: Generate new scaffolds for KRAS
cases.why: 'fold' lives inside 'scaffold'; a keyword must match only where a word starts.

cases.question: Anchor on the co-crystal structure of CDK2
cases.why: 'Co' is cobalt and also the first half of 'co-crystal'.

cases.question: target prediction
cases.why: The reported failure: the bare phrase was refused as unsupported, then routed to hit discovery. A compound with an unknown target is the opposite job from finding ligands for a known one.

cases.question: my phenotypic screen gave a hit and I do not know what it binds
cases.why: Names a screen and a hit, which is hit-discovery vocabulary, but asks for deconvolution. Checks the screening words do not pull it back.

cases.question: which target should I pick for Parkinsons disease
cases.why: Guards the boundary the other way: choosing a target for a disease is triage, not deconvolution of a compound.
